judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain claims-made notice; the only softness is 'ERODE THE LIMITS', which the operative Section III.D and Endorsement 6 spell out precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says claims must be reported 'DURING THE POLICY PERIOD' while Insuring Agreements I.A/I.B and Section VIII permit reporting during an 'extended reporting period', a modest tension a court could be asked to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration statement listing the documents that constitute the policy; nothing in it carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the endorsement structure and IX.K (Changes and Assignment); no competing integration or priority-of-documents clause exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical is garbled ('Item. 2.a and/or litem, 3.a., above., whichever is earlier') and '100 % minimum-earned' as a percentage figure is stated oddly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IX.A.3 says the 'premium percentage identified in Item 5.' is the minimum earned premium and then provides for pro rata earning of 'remaining unearned premium' and a refund, which cannot be reconciled with a 100% minimum-earned premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical to the Declarations notice; standard claims-made language with no term needing construction beyond OCR noise ('WHAT 1S').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same tension with I.A/I.B and Section VIII extended reporting period reporting windows as the Declarations notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple interpretive convention that quoted words are defined in Section V.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several quoted terms are in fact undefined ('covered operations' in Endorsement 6.I.E/F, 'loss' in Endorsement 6.IV.F), so the convention does not hold across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate consideration and reliance clause; nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with IX.F Representations and the Fraud or Misrepresentation exclusion; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in conditioning coverage on the Declarations identifying the coverage; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplemental Coverages added by Endorsements 3, 4 and 13 are not 'identified on the Declarations', so the lead-in sits awkwardly with them even though Item 4 refers to Supplemental Coverages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period' is a demanding and contestable trigger for a continuing condition, and 'arising out of' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 5.II (retroactive-date version) and Endorsement 10.I (transportation version), which are inconsistent with each other and leave the operative Coverage A text uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains the typo 'nolicy period' and pairs 'first commenced, in whole or part, prior to the policy period' with a requirement that discovery occur during the period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Coverage A (c008) the two coverages divide conditions by commencement date; the Endorsement 5 retroactive-date rewrite of Coverage A blurs that division for scheduled locations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and internally consistent SIR attachment language; 'satisfactory evidence' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.AA, III.D and IX.D (bankruptcy does not relieve the SIR obligation); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical per-condition limit keyed to Item 2.b.; nothing ambiguous except the familiar 'same, continuous, repeated, or related' aggregation phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I deletes and replaces this subsection, dropping 'legal defense expense' from it, so the base text no longer operates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward aggregate limit provision keyed to Item 2.c.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2.c is $9,000,000 while Item 4's Total Policy Aggregate is $7,000,000, and this subsection is also replaced by Endorsement 6.I.D — a genuine numerical incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain per-condition limit for Coverage B keyed to Item 3.b.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I.E deletes and replaces it with text adding the undefined qualifier 'resulting from covered operations', which narrows it in a way the base policy nowhere supports.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain aggregate limit for Coverage B keyed to Item 3.c.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Replaced by Endorsement 6.I.F, which introduces the undefined term 'covered operations'; the base and endorsed versions cover different ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to Subsections C., D., E. and F., above' is odd for a provision that purports to be the overall maximum, since it makes the cap subordinate to the very limits it is meant to cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 4's $7,000,000 total aggregate is smaller than the Coverage A aggregate ($9,000,000) plus Coverage B aggregate ($5,000,000) and smaller than the BI sublimit-plus-limits stack, an inconsistency across the Declarations and Endorsements 3, 6 and 13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long deeming provision with OCR noise; 'continuous, repeated, or related' is the sort of phrase courts routinely construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The closing words 'no other policy shall respond' purport to control other policies (this is a renewal of PPL G24551532 001) and sit uneasily with IX.H Other Insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear right and duty to defend with a defined endpoint; 'to which this insurance applies' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II.A deletes and replaces this subsection with a version keyed to the Dedicated Defense Sublimit, so the base version is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives the Insurer 'the right to select legal counsel' and then says selection 'shall not be done without the consent of the insured' — the two sentences pull against each other on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F gives the first named insured the selection right after exhaustion of the defense sublimit, and IX.M's consent standard overlays this; the interaction is workable but not seamless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'right and the duty to retain a qualified environmental consultant' coupled with a consent requirement is clear enough, and 'emergency response' is defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.III deletes and replaces this exact subsection, so the base text does not operate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence; erosion of limits and application to the SIR are both stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II.D deletes and replaces it, redirecting erosion to the Dedicated Defense Sublimit and Item 4 only, which changes the result for Items 2 and 3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not impose any additional unreasonable burdens on the insured' is a vague qualifier on a consequential consent-to-settle mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F restates a version of the same mechanism with garbled wording ('for which it is not which is acceptable'), leaving two overlapping settlement provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence limiting coverage to pollution conditions located and claims made in the United States; 'located' is the only soft word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Service of Suit endorsement contemplates a Canadian-resident insured, and Endorsement 8 separately requires US-located disposal sites; minor but not conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential but plain: additional insureds are those endorsed as such, with rights limited to the endorsement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 2 supplies the schedule and the vicarious-liability limit, which is consistent with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but conventional bodily injury definition; 'prospective medical monitoring costs' is unusual yet defined by purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the Employers Liability exclusion and Section VII.B; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Mutually agreed upon by the Insurer and the insured' as an element of a definition creates a potential veto, and 'ordinary ambient indoor air ecology' is vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 removes fungi and legionella from 'pollution condition' and adds a Fungi and Legionella exclusion, leaving this definition (and its use in 'remediation costs') largely orphaned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'written assertion of a legal right' with a non-exhaustive 'including, but not limited to' list invites an ejusdem generis argument about what else counts as a claim.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 8.II and Endorsement 11.II, which give different limiting text; which controls is not stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and closed definition ending at unloading; 'other conveyance' is a catch-all after a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.II deletes Subsection E entirely and substitutes 'Transportation', so 'contingent transportation' ceases to exist even though the base Vehicles exclusion still refers to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short three-limb definition; the OCR has dropped the '1.' numbering but the sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.I and Endorsement 11.I each purport to delete Subsection F 'in its entirety' and replace it with different text, and both refer to an Automatic Acquisition endorsement that is not attached.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A hard 72-hour window and an 'imminent and substantial threat' standard; the latter is a familiar but workable phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used as an exception in III.C, VI.H and VII.C consistently; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise: the obligation must be 'explicitly included' in a scheduled contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement is attached, so the carve-back to the Contractual Liability exclusion (VI.B) has nothing to operate on — a dangling cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Including 'guidance document' and non-binding 'guidance' within 'law' is genuinely contestable, and the definition governs what remediation is 'required'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds directly into 'remediation costs' (V.Y) and 'government action' (V.M); the fit is consistent even if the term is broad.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a claim first made against the insured during or subsequent to the end of the policy period' is one clause doing two different jobs and reads awkwardly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Insuring Agreements require the claim to be 'first made ... during the policy period', and VIII.B deems ERP claims made on the last day of the period, so this definition appears to extend coverage the Insuring Agreements do not grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but definite allocation of agency and payment responsibility to the first named insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.S, IX.A and IX.G's carve-out for 'obligations specifically assigned to the first named insured'; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential ('byproducts produced or released by fungi') but the meaning is not really in doubt.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 deletes fungi from 'pollution condition' and excludes fungi altogether, so this definition survives only to service an exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite, keyed to action under 'environmental law'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.D 'claim' and V.I; nothing pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'intentional placement' by a third party, with an open-ended irritant list; the three conditions are cumulative and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Carried forward unchanged into Endorsement 12's replacement of 'pollution condition'; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition uses 'insured' inside the definition of 'insured' ('employee of ... any insured'), which is circular, and 'within the scope of his or her duties' is a stock but contestable qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth makes the Insured vs. Insured exclusion (VI.I) very wide and sits against the Separation of Insureds condition (IX.G), which carves that exclusion out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable' legal costs is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinated with III.B, III.D and Endorsement 6; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'greater than specified quantities' does not say specified by whom or where, a small but real gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only within 'pollution condition' and 'illicit abandonment'; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Anchored to two named federal statutes; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in W.3 and N; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear: same rights as the first named insured except those reserved in Subsection K.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 1 schedules Farm Nutrients LLC, and IX.G applies the policy separately to each named insured; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list closed by 'and other such resources', a general catch-all after specifics that could be argued either way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12.III sublimits natural resource damage claims to $500,000 while V.X folds NRD into 'property damage'; workable but layered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very broad on its face: any site 'not owned or operated by an insured' that ever received insured waste.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.II deletes and replaces this definition with a far narrower, condition-laden version, so the base text does not operate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 2 is grammatically mangled ('the period of time following the closing date ... or, as applicable, through the applicable expiration date'), leaving its start and end genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Automatic Acquisition and Due Diligence Endorsement is attached, so limb 2 is inoperative; limb 1 and the cancellation limb fit IX.A.2's deeming of cancellation as the end of the policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'irritant, contaminant, or pollutant' following an illustrative list is the single most litigated phrase in pollution coverage, and its reach over a biological agent is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12.I deletes this subsection in its entirety and replaces it (dropping fungi/legionella and excluding odor), yet V.C and V.Y still assume fungi remediation is covered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated limbs, each specific; 'diminished value of tangible property owned by a third-party' is unusual but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with the First-Party Property Damage exclusion (VI.F) and the NRD sublimit in Endorsement 12.III without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to the extent required by environmental law' is the classic battleground over what remediation is compensable, and 'reasonable expenses' adds a second soft standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fungi/legionella sentence assumes coverage for fungi remediation that Endorsement 12's Fungi and Legionella exclusion removes entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any employee ... responsible for environmental affairs, control, or compliance' has no clear boundary, and knowledge of such a person drives the Known Conditions and UST exclusions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in VI.G, VI.J, VI.K and VI.P consistently; no contradiction, though its breadth magnifies those exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure pointer to Declarations Items 2.d and 3.d; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 adds a Catastrophe Management-Specific SIR, which the closing words ('or as otherwise designated by endorsement') accommodate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'activities against persons, organizations or property of any nature' with 'commission or threat of a dangerous act' is broad and subjective, and OCR page-footer text is embedded mid-clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the War or Terrorism exclusion (VI.R); no conflict located.
